claim: A turn basis that pins CognitiveFrame + graph epoch + activation epoch before workspace competition reduces mixed-version cognitive episodes relative to sequential latest reads.
counter: At real FRANK update rates, retries may be rare enough that pinning overhead is not worthwhile.
test: Live per-source epoch audit: latest+validate vs pin+read under identical workload; measure mixed-basis rejection, retry rate, p99, retained-version memory.

claim: RCU/MVCC-like immutable epoch pinning outperforms check-and-retry above a workload-dependent update/read crossover.
counter: Epoch retention/reclamation costs dominate even at high update rates.
test: Sweep update rate, read span, Assembly lifetime and graph size; compare p99 latency, memory, failed reads and reclamation lag.

claim: A truthful sparse latent field improves action/recall on cases where query-only FRANK fails to initiate memory retrieval, beyond no-field and shuffled-field controls.
counter: Any benefit is merely extra visible context or associative noise.
test: No field vs truthful field vs relation-shuffled vs temporal-shuffled field with identical visible facts, order and token budget.

claim: ClayGraph should not be the universal hot path: exact/local facts should bypass graph traversal and associative/multihop cases should escalate conditionally.
counter: A resident graph is fast enough and yields better uniform behavior.
test: Exact/keyword baseline vs resident graph vs adaptive escalation across exact, associative, multihop and conflict queries; measure recall, precision, p95/p99, token cost, false association.

claim: A deterministic reader ABI compiled from canonical ClayCode/ClayGraph semantics reduces unsafe authority/freshness errors on target Qwen4B compared with raw compact ClayCode while retaining part of the token savings.
counter: Compiler projection distorts semantics or structured format itself causes equal/larger model bias.
test: Tokenizer-matched target 4B factorial: canonical JSON, readable ClayCode, compact raw, compiled explicit ABI; score semantic accuracy, unsafe ACCEPT, tokens, latency; randomize order/format.

claim: GWT causal attribution requires separate receipts for transport, projection integrity, reconstruction/uptake, effect and outcome/re-entry.
counter: Projection receipt adds observability cost without changing attribution conclusions.
test: Correct vs scrambled projection while holding transport constant; measure uptake and downstream effect/outcome continuity.

claim: ClayGraph activation and GWT ignition are orthogonal causal variables whose interaction can be estimated factorially.
counter: They collapse to one salience mechanism in practice.
test: GRAPH_PRIOR truthful/shuffled/none x WORKSPACE winner truthful/shuffled/none x reentry truthful/shuffled/none with matched projection content/order.

claim: Lateral inhibition/saturation control prevents noisy hubs from monopolizing the latent field without materially reducing useful recall.
counter: Inhibition suppresses genuinely central memories and hurts recall more than it reduces noise.
test: Decay-only vs decay+inhibition vs hub caps across synthetic and live query sets; measure hub share, recall, false association, activation entropy, latency.

claim: Adaptive overlay compaction based on changed fraction/read volume/query tax beats always-overlay and always-rebuild policies.
counter: Policy complexity outweighs small wins; fixed rebuild threshold is sufficient.
test: Replay real FRANK/ClayGraph update/read traces through all three policies; measure publication latency, query p99, memory and integrity failures.

claim: Canonical n-ary semantics plus explicit relation-instance role-labelled reader projection is a better small-model interface than naive pairwise flattening.
counter: Target 4B prefers simpler pairwise syntax despite information loss.
test: Randomize role order; remove positional leakage; equal-semantics target 4B role-binding benchmark.

claim: Sparse event-driven latent state plus bounded compiled Assembly is especially favorable on Android/edge compared with per-turn LLM graph reranking.
counter: Memory bookkeeping and graph retention erase energy/latency advantages.
test: Target-device energy/thermal/p99 benchmark with no-field, sparse field, and LLM-rerank arms.

claim: Outcome-conditioned plasticity can improve future latent memory salience without granting authority if updates are receipt-bound and lesion-tested.
counter: Plasticity reinforces self-generated errors and creates runaway feedback.
test: Truthful outcome receipts vs shuffled outcomes vs no plasticity; measure recurrence, error reinforcement, OOD stability and rollback.
